- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–5 days, especially if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment history shows repeated high-low oscillation, model tends to lag; apply 1–3 day lag correction by shifting forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–4% below true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, apply mean reversion rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast each day until convergence.
- For sentiment >0.6 and price >70, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 10% above prior peak to avoid runaway inflation.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to adjust; apply 2–4% downward correction to next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment shift.
